correctness.rationale: I independently diagonalized the noisy two-site bridge Gram matrix into even and odd modes and integrated the squared kernel projections. This gives the displayed gain and, after differentiation and the gap-to-odds change, the exact sextic. The negative constant and positive degrees 3 through 6 give one coefficient sign change: when the linear coefficient is positive, eta>1/2 and the quadratic coefficient is positive as well. Descartes and opposite signs at z=0 and 1/2 give a unique simple root and a global gain maximum, against both endpoint and coincident symmetric designs. The simple root at z=1/2 at zero noise gives the -2/3 small-noise slope. At high noise set w=1/eta and z=cw: w^2 P_{1/w}(cw) is polynomial in (c,w) with limit 16c-2, giving a unique positive branch near c=1/8. At any repeated site the gain is increasing in its bridge variance and is maximal at the midpoint; the symmetric gain has strictly positive right derivative there. This proves strict domination of even off-center repeated sites.
